podcast.title: "Fabulous Whalers" Distinction
podcast.body: The group is often referred to as "The Fabulous Whalers" to differentiate them from Bob Marley's later, more renowned group of the same name. "The Whalers, who are often referred to as the Fabulous Whalers, distinguished them from Bob Marley's later more famous group"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Rockin' Robin's Post-Music Career and Death
podcast.body: After his music career, Rockin' Robin became an associate professor of biochemistry. He tragically died young in a car crash in 1967. "Rockin Robbins went on to become an associate professor of biochemistry, before dying far too young in a car crash in 1967."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Spanish Castle Residency and Jimi Hendrix Influence
podcast.body: The Whalers held a residency at the local venue, The Spanish Castle. Their exceptional live shows there were later commemorated by regular audience member Jimi Hendrix in his song "Spanish Castle Magic." "The shows at that venue were so good that several years later, one of the regular audience members, Jimmy Hendrix, would commemorate them in the song Spanish Castle Map Jic."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Tacoma Origin and Scene
podcast.body: The Whalers originated from Tacoma, a city known for its robust instrumental guitar band scene, producing bands with a sound similar to The Ventures. "were a group from Tacoma, which had a strong instrumental guitar band scene. Most famously the ventures came from Tacoma, and a lot of the bands in the area sounded like that."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
